source_review.notes: Reviewed Okasaki's primary thesis, queue/deque paper, and persistence-aware amortization chapter; the Archive of Formal Proofs Hood-Melville development; the Hinze-Paterson finger-tree paper; the Kaplan-Tarjan technical report; the 2025 verified catenable-deque paper; and current Clojure PersistentQueue source. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked Nil/Cons, front/rear queue state, abstraction sequence, stored lengths, potential, work, suspension, schedule, roots, version DAG, and reachability notation.
Checked FIFO queue, deque, priority queue, stream, persistent value, and durable message queue remain distinct abstractions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Real-time data-structure steps are explicitly distinguished from wall-clock deadlines.

evidence: Recomputed the eight executable queue versions from empty through linear, branch, and dequeue histories.
Recomputed q3 as alpha,beta,gamma; q4 as beta,gamma; q5 as beta,gamma,delta; q6 as alpha,beta,xray; and q7 as beta.
Recomputed the shared-list example as eight logical occurrences and five unique nodes, and the persistent attack as Theta(k n) reverse work.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite tuple identities and lengths are not allocator-byte or asymptotic-performance measurements.

evidence: Verified list persistence inductively from immutable Cons construction and unchanged tails.
Verified enqueue from reverse(Cons(x,R)) = reverse(R) ++ [x], dequeue from front removal, and normalization from equivalent abstraction sequences.
Verified the linear amortized argument charges each rear cell once, while branching from a pre-rotation root invalidates reuse of the same potential.
Verified memoization can share delayed work only with deterministic once-publication, and a real-time schedule additionally needs a deadline/progress proof.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Semantic correctness, linear-history amortization, persistent amortization, and worst-case bounds are separate claims.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, normalization boundary, alternating operations, long rear/front, repeated branches, equal-content roots, and mutable payloads.
Reviewed call-by-name repeated work, thunk exceptions/retry, concurrent force, reentrancy, abandoned evaluating state, length overflow, recursive stack exhaustion, and arena/refcount/GC retention.

Reviewed writer CAS loss/retry, root/iterator pinning, hostile depth and graph serialization, corrupt references, schema migration, durable-publication category errors, quotas, and sensitive histories.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Quotas cover size, roots, branches, reader age, thunk work/depth, element/live/retained bytes, operation time, and serialized output.

evidence: The executable checks exact front/rear lengths and the invariant that every nonempty normalized queue has a front cell across eight retained versions.
It compares every logical queue with an independent expected tuple and checks old roots, branch isolation, front sharing, and equal-but-nonidentical reversed nodes.
The chapter specifies additional schedule, memo, lifetime, concurrency, serialization, and durable-publication invariants separately.
invariant_checking.notes: The trace validates a finite eager two-list queue, not a lazy, persistence-amortized, real-time, concurrent, or durable implementation.

evidence: Reviewed abstract list/FIFO semantics, suffix sharing, append, two-list derivation, abstraction/normalization, and error behavior.
Reviewed linear and persistent amortization boundaries, memoized laziness, schedules, strict rotation state, deques, concatenation, and finger trees.
Reviewed failure, reclamation, concurrency, serialization, durable boundaries, security/resource controls, property/fault testing, and benchmarks.
proof_review.notes: Published algorithms are cited rather than claiming the chapter sketch reproduces their complete machine-checked proofs.

evidence: List and basic queue induction, the branching counterexample, memo assumptions, and real-time deadline obligation are separately labeled and scoped.
The strict state-machine exercise explicitly withholds a bound absent a completed deadline proof.
The executable is labeled finite semantic/structural evidence and disclaims asymptotic, lazy, concurrent, and durability proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No queue representation is claimed universally optimal.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact thirteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under Python 3.14.4.
It emits evidence=finite_persistent_two_list_queue_trace and reproduces FIFO order, normalization, persistence, branching, and selected identity relations.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed draft module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No asymptotic timing, branching attack instrumentation, memoized force, real-time schedule, fault injection, refcount/GC/arena, concurrency, serialization, crash recovery, security, or production tail behavior was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Progresses from immutable list semantics through two-list FIFO derivation, the persistence/amortization conflict, lazy and scheduled repairs, representation alternatives, lifecycle concerns, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed total empty APIs, payload ownership, length overflow, lazy failure and once-publication, rotation states, roots/readers/retention, refcount/GC/arenas, atomic latest-root publication, backpressure/category boundaries, logical serialization, durable recovery, quotas, migrations, faults, and tail metrics.

pedagogical_review.notes: Uses the simplest persistent spine before exposing the subtle branching-amortization failure, includes a reproducible version trace, ten varied examples, and five graduate exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Okasaki, Hood/Melville, Hinze/Paterson, Kaplan/Tarjan, Gómez-Londoño/AFP, Viennot/Wendling/Guéneau/Pottier, Clojure, programming-languages, concurrency, security, performance, reliability, storage, formal-methods, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite eager trace prove neither arbitrary list/queue implementations, deep payload persistence, persistent amortized or worst-case bounds, correct call-by-need/memo publication, Hood-Melville or Kaplan-Tarjan algorithms, finger-tree invariants, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, refcount/GC/epoch/arena correctness, thread safety/linearizability/progress, channel/backpressure behavior, graph serialization, durable broker/crash recovery/delivery semantics, hostile-input security, production memory/cache/GC/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
